I will not be voting for the House Republicans' temporary government funding bill AKA a full-year Continuing Resolution because it hands unchecked power to billionaires while stripping Congress of its ability to direct critical funding for public health, infrastructure, and working-class support. 

This isn’t about fiscal responsibility—it’s a reckless power grab that prioritizes the wealthy over working families, and I refuse to stand by while our communities suffer.

The 44% cut in Army Corps funding proposed by House Republicans will have real consequences on the environment, commerce, and public health.

That means sites like the West Lake Landfill—a radioactive waste site in our own backyard—will face delays in cleanup. Managing disaster risk and hazardous waste shouldn’t take a back seat.

What’s more important than our health and safety? Make it make sense!
Lives, health, and futures are on the line. Swipe to discover why protecting Medicaid matters ⬇️ https://t.co/VBL1x8yZ5E

Republicans want to slash up to $900 billion from Medicaid by imposing “per capita caps,” limiting funds regardless of growing needs. This would devastate health coverage for millions relying on Medicaid expansion.
 
We must protect healthcare access, not dismantle it

Fifteen years ago today, the Affordable Care Act became law, expanding health coverage to millions—including thousands of St. Louisans. As we celebrate this milestone, we must recognize that folks are still falling through the cracks.

Working families shouldn’t have to ration insulin, skip doctor visits, or drown in medical debt. Healthcare must be affordable, accessible, and guaranteed. That’s the future I’m fighting for

https://t.co/2mTzibnCvi

You can’t claim to care about public health or education while yanking $255 million from Missouri communities midstream.

That money was already at work—supporting health clinics, school ventilation upgrades, and basic services families rely on.

This isn’t cleanup. It’s sabotage

My new legislative package aims to incentivize local governments to reduce jail populations and invest in alternatives to incarceration such as mental health treatment, addiction services, job training, and housing.

Too many lives have been derailed by low-level, nonviolent charge. Too many tax dollars wasted on a system that doesn’t work. 

It’s time to build safer, stronger communities—that invests in people and not prisons

Confirmed cases of measles have now reached St. Louis. With measles, one case can expose dozens—especially children, the immunocompromised, and those without access to care.

We need robust public health funding, stronger immunization outreach, and a national strategy to fight medical misinformation. Lives are at stake. This is the cost of inaction.

Marshaun Futrell Jr. was just 11 years old. A football star. A son. A big brother. Now his name joins a heartbreaking list—20 kids shot in the St. Louis region this year alone.

Gun violence is a public health emergency, and I won’t stop fighting until we treat it like one. Enough is enough.

I’m a hard NO on this “big beautiful bill" that would gut Medicaid and SNAP—just so the ultra-wealthy can get another tax cut.

I won’t support a plan that takes food off families’ tables and health care from seniors just to hand out more breaks to billionaires. People in Missouri didn’t send me here to play games—they sent me to stand up for them.

And that’s exactly what I’m doing.

Thank you to Secretary of the VA Doug Collins for visiting John Cochran VA Medical Center this afternoon. Our Veterans deserve the best healthcare available. I appreciate the opportunity to work together to ensure that outcome. https://t.co/IDyAbvlihq

Today, I introduced the Public Safety and Mental Health Reporting Act—a bill to improve transparency by collecting comprehensive data on law enforcement interactions involving individuals experiencing mental illness.

Recognizing the connection between mental health and public safety is long overdue. Without real data, we can’t develop solutions that protect both our communities and our officers. This bill ensures accountability, safeguards privacy, and lays the foundation for evidence-based policies that meet the moment.

Big news for public health in St. Louis County: our Department of Public Health just earned FQHC Look-Alike status—unlocking millions in new funding, expanded care access, and critical support for underserved communities.

Proud to celebrate this major step toward a healthier St. Louis.

Every day, our communities see the crucial intersection of mental health and law enforcement. Without comprehensive data, we cannot effectively address these encounters and ensure the safety and well-being of all involved. 

This legislation is about transparency, accountability, and better-informed policies to protect both citizens and officers.

I simply cannot reconcile being given the responsibility of serving in Congress and using it to take health care from 17 million poor and working Americans, just to give billionaires a tax cut. 

As a man of faith, we were taught to care for the most vulnerable among us, not to turn our backs on them. The sheer immorality and greed of it should haunt every person who votes yes.

Under the Republican budget bill:
- 500+ nursing homes face closure
- 300+ hospitals face closure
- 270,000 veterans & foster youth lose food aid
- $1T ripped from health care

Missouri families deserve better than handouts for billionaires and hardship for everyone else.

This bill steals from health care, poisons the air, jacks up our grocery bills, and mortgages our kids’ future so a handful of politicians keep their Mar-a-Lago invitations. That’s the real headline.

I’m voting HELL NO on this heist, and we have to keep calling out every lie. Don’t be gullible. Stay engaged. Stay in the fight. 💪

I voted no because Trump’s Big Ugly Bill was cruel—ripping health care away from 17 million Americans and over 260,000 Missourians, including seniors, children, and pregnant moms, while handing tax breaks to billionaires. Not to mention slashing food assistance for millions of people in need. 

Buried in that same bill was RECA, which I’ve fought for from the beginning, and I’m relieved to see the long overdue compensation finally moving forward for those exposed to radiation right here at home. But make no mistake—the fight is just beginning to restore Medicaid, SNAP, and undo the utter cruelty packed into the Big Ugly Bill.

Spoke at the 1st Annual Kustawi Summit this morning: a powerful gathering focused on breaking the stigma around mental health and uplifting our African immigrant communities. From healthcare to small business, your contributions make St. Louis stronger. My commitment is to keep fighting for the policies that help you not just live, but thrive.

On the 60th anniversary of Medicaid, I brought together providers, advocates, and health care leaders from all across Missouri for a roundtable discussion on the devastating impact of the Big Ugly Bill—which adds burdens on already strained health systems without providing the resources to meet those demands. Providers made it clear that these cuts will limit access to care, worsen outcomes, and place working families and low-income communities at even greater risk.

Hearing directly from those on the front lines, the message was unanimous: seniors, children, and people with disabilities will pay the price of these cuts. This rollback on essential care is nothing but cruel. I’m committed to standing with the people of St. Louis to protect the care they depend on.

Affordable housing is one of the biggest challenges we face; it touches everything: health, education, safety, economic opportunity, etc.. If people don’t have a stable and safe place to live, nothing else can fall in place.

I visited Marquette Homes with local leaders to celebrate the more than 50 new living spaces it will bring to St. Louis!

I introduced the Healthy Servicemembers Act with @RepYassAnsari to make sure military families aren’t left to suffer from unsafe housing. Our bill requires the Department of Defense to screen and track health conditions linked to substandard housing and raise awareness about available resources.

Too many families have had their health put at risk. If you serve this country, you deserve a safe home—and accountability when problems arise.

Health equity isn’t just some slogan. It means every child, regardless of background, gets the care they deserve. When folks try to dismiss health equity, what they’re really saying is not all kids matter. I won’t let that slide. https://t.co/Hc0X2vrHhf

If we're serious about public safety, we have to be serious about the solutions. Ignoring mental health and defaulting to harsher prosecutions hasn’t made us safer; it’s made the problem worse. My career has always been about holding serious and violent offenders accountable—but looking for alternatives to incarceration for low-level nonviolent offenders and addressing root causes.
The claim that Tylenol causes autism has not been substantiated. This is what happens when a quack with no expertise is put in charge of our health. https://t.co/K8FpIf7uxT
